target_description: Photo with school friends at a restaurant
remembered_before_retrieval: friends; approximately 2021; restaurant context; birthday; red wall
observed_sequence: 1. searched "birthday" | 2. results contained many unrelated birthday photos | 3. refined by searching a friend's name | 4. manually scrolled | 5. eventually found the target
failure_stage_reason: The user possessed multiple contextual and visual memories but struggled to translate them into a sufficiently discriminating query.
hardest_moment_quote: I knew what the photo looked like but didn't know what to type
researcher_observation: User began with a broad event query despite remembering richer contextual and visual clues. After noisy results, he refined using a friend's name and eventually fell back to scrolling.

target_description: Specific family photo from his sister's wedding
observed_sequence: 1. searched "wedding" | 2. results contained many unrelated wedding cards, screenshots and other wedding-related content | 3. refined using sister's name | 4. manually scrolled | 5. eventually found the target
first_result_quality: noisy / mixed with irrelevant wedding-related content
failure_stage_reason: The user provided a meaningful event query, but the returned set was noisy and did not efficiently surface the specific target.
hardest_moment_quote: I remember when the photo was taken but there were a lot of photos taken so it was hard to find this exact one
researcher_observation: Initial search produced broad wedding-related content including cards and screenshots. Even with remembered time and event context, locating the exact target required further refinement and manual browsing. The user's final comment also indicates later evaluation difficulty among many photos from the same event.

target_description: Photo from a football team match
remembered_before_retrieval: football fixture / match context; football team; knew approximately what the target photo looked like
observed_sequence: 1. searched "football" | 2. results contained many football-related images because the participant has many football photos | 3. refined using his football team's name | 4. manually scrolled | 5. eventually found the target
first_result_quality: relevant but too broad / too many similar candidates
failure_stage_reason: The user knew the target context and appearance but initially could not formulate a query specific enough to distinguish it from many other football photos.
hardest_moment_quote: I knew what the photo looked like but didn't know what to type as I have many football pics as I am a football fan
researcher_observation: User's first query represented the broad category rather than the distinctive memory. The result set contained many plausible football photos, creating additional evaluation effort before refinement and scrolling.

first_result_quality: relevant category but too many similar candidates
refinement_description: narrowed using the month associated with the screenshot
failure_stage_reason: The participant reached the correct screenshot category, but the large number of plausible candidates made identifying the exact screenshot difficult.
hardest_moment_quote: I remember when the screenshot was taken but there were a lot of photos taken so it was hard to find this exact one
researcher_observation: The participant knew the target was a screenshot and entered the correct category, but category-level retrieval still produced too many plausible candidates. He eventually narrowed the search using remembered temporal context.

remembered_before_retrieval: 2022; graduation event; the photo was personally memorable
observed_sequence: 1. navigated using the year | 2. used year/month chronological browsing | 3. found the target photo | 4. afterwards saved it to Favourites
failure_stage_reason: The participant remembered useful temporal and event context, navigated directly using year/month, and found the target in approximately two minutes without needing a failed query or recovery attempt.
hardest_moment_quote: I remember this photo and was easy to find as it hold many memories, i just used by year and month to scroll and found it , was easy
researcher_observation: Manual scrolling was the participant's intended retrieval method, not a fallback after failure.
